summary: A will must leave at least two thirds of the inheritance to the testator's children (including disabled and posthumous), disabled spouse and parents who would be heirs (Civil Code art. 522.3). Inheritance is governed by the law of permanent residence, and Mongolian law governs Mongolian land. I found no trust law, and foundations are for public benefit.
reserved_share: Children, disabled spouse, parents and other lawful successors: no less than two thirds of the inheritance when property is willed away from them (Civil Code art. 522.3).
foreign_law_note: Civil Code art. 552: inheritance relations are governed by the law of the country of permanent residence of the successor (as translated), and the testator's capacity and the will's form by the law of the testator's residence. Inheritance of immovables in Mongolia is governed by Mongolian law (art. 552.4). There is no right to choose a national law.
trust_note: Not on the HCCH status table. The Civil Code has no trust; a lawyer directory mentions a trust law but I could not verify. Foundations (arts. 36-38) are legal persons without members, created by donors to pursue publicly beneficial goals, with a donor governing body.
open_questions: The English translation of art. 552.1 says 'successor' where 'deceased' may be meant; check the Mongolian text.
Confirm no trust statute exists and whether a foundation may benefit a family.
Check for amendments to the 2002 Civil Code since 2002.
